# requireUrl

<link-summary>Returns the value as a URL, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireUrl() — Returns the value as a URL, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/url</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireUrl(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a valid URL."): string;
```

An `http`, `https` or `ftp` URL with something after the scheme and no whitespace anywhere. A bare host such as `"example.com"` is not one.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                          | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                            | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid URL."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a URL.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition               |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a URL. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireUrl("https://example.com"); // => "https://example.com"
requireUrl("http://example.com/a?b=1"); // => "http://example.com/a?b=1"
requireUrl("example.com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireUrl("https://"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
